notice: RN bank batch 155: Case studies: defense mechanisms after a heart attack and a school-age child with new type 1 diabetes, with four standalone items. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: A client who had a kidney transplant 6 weeks ago calls the transplant clinic. Using the note, fill in the bowtie: the most likely problem in the middle, two actions to take now on the left and two parameters to monitor on the right.

actions.text: Tell the client to come in today for labs and possible biopsy
Advise doubling tacrolimus tonight to catch up
Advise ibuprofen for the graft pain
Reassure and recheck at the routine visit

rationale.correct: Missed immunosuppressants with a tender graft and less urine suggests rejection.

perOption.c1: Fever, graft tenderness, less urine and rising creatinine after missed doses.
perOption.c2: Does not explain a tender graft and missed tacrolimus.
perOption.c4: Doses were missed; the level is low.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize and act on transplant rejection.

exhibits.title: Phone call
exhibits.body: Missed tacrolimus for 3 days (ran out). Temperature 37.9 C, tender over the graft, passing less urine, weight up 1.5 kg. Yesterday's creatinine 2.1 (baseline 1.1). Tacrolimus level 2 ng/mL.

questions.stem: For each age group, choose the most typical type of play.

cells.text: Shakes a rattle and watches it
Plays near another child with similar toys, without interacting
Plays pretend house with other children loosely
Joins a team with rules and roles

rationale.correct: Play develops from solitary to parallel, associative and cooperative.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Play room
exhibits.body: Children of different ages on the pediatric unit.

questions.stem: On an inpatient mental health unit at 0700, four clients need the nurse. Which client should the nurse see first?

options.text: A client on lithium who has vomited twice and has a coarse tremor and slurred speech
A client with schizophrenia who refuses breakfast because the food is "poisoned"
A client with anorexia who wants to skip the morning weigh-in
A client with depression who is tearful after a phone call

rationale.correct: Lithium toxicity is a medical emergency.

perOption.a: Signs of lithium toxicity are a medical emergency.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize clients on a mental health unit.

questions.stem: The school nurse plans teaching for 16-year-olds who recently got driver's licenses. Which topics address the leading cause of death in this age group? Select all that apply.

options.text: Always wear a seat belt, including in the back seat
Do not text or use the phone while driving
Never drive after alcohol or cannabis, or ride with an impaired driver
Limit teen passengers as graduated licensing laws require
Speeding is safe on empty roads at night
Energy drinks are a safe way to stay awake on long drives

rationale.correct: Motor vehicle crashes lead deaths in teens; belts, no phones, no impairment and passenger limits help.

perOption.e: Speed and night driving raise risk.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the behaviors that are defense mechanisms.

cells: Asks to be fed and bathed

rationale.correct: Several defense mechanisms protect the client from the fear of the MI.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: For each behavior, indicate the defense mechanism.

rows.text: Refuses to believe the heart attack happened
Takes anger out on the spouse
Discusses lab values without showing feeling
Acts younger and more dependent
"I'll be at work Monday"

rationale.correct: Naming the defense helps choose the response.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: Denial is a problem when it {{b1}}, so the nurse should {{b2}}.

options.text: stops the client following life-saving treatment
gently present the facts and connect treatment to the client's goals
argue until the client admits the MI
tell the client they will die soon

rationale.correct: Address denial when it blocks treatment, gently and with the client's goals.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which responses fit the client's defenses? Select all that apply.

options.text: "These medicines help you get back to work."
"Stop pretending this heart attack didn't happen to you."
Do all care for the client to reduce stress

rationale.correct: Link to goals, name feelings and encourage independence.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which referrals should the nurse arrange before discharge? Select all that apply.

options.text: A counselor or support group for coping
No referrals until the denial resolves
A referral only for the spouse

rationale.correct: Rehab, depression screening, coping support and risk reduction.
references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.stem: At the 2-week visit, for each statement, indicate whether it shows healthy coping or needs follow-up.

rows.text: "I was scared. I'm taking my pills and going to rehab."
"I've cut my work hours while I recover."
"My wife and I talked about how frightened we were."
"I stopped the metoprolol because I feel fine."
"I can't sleep and don't enjoy anything anymore."

rationale.correct: Most coping is healthy; stopping medicines and low mood need follow-up.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that shape teaching for this school-age child.

cells: Likes to learn how things work

rationale.correct: School-age children learn by doing and care about fitting in.

perOption.r1: Concrete learning; teach with hands-on practice.
perOption.r5: Confirms diabetes; not a teaching factor.

questions.stem: For each diabetes task, indicate who usually does it at age 8 with supervision.

rows.text: Check own fingerstick glucose
Recognize and report feeling low
Choose snacks from a list
Calculate and decide insulin doses
Give glucagon when the child is unconscious

columns.text: The child can do it with supervision

rationale.correct: School-age children take on tasks gradually with adult oversight.

questions.stem: Which parts of the school plan should the nurse help arrange? Select all that apply.

Trained staff who can give glucagon
Permission to check glucose and eat snacks in class
Fast sugar kept with the child and in the classroom
Keep diabetes secret from the teacher

exhibits.title: Day 2 after an anterior MI
exhibits.body: A 52-year-old business owner had a stent placed after an anterior myocardial infarction. The client walks around the unit making work calls and says, "It was just indigestion; I'm fine."

rows.label: Day 2
cells: "I don't need these heart pills; I'll be at work Monday."

rows.label: Day 3
cells: Shouts at the spouse about the parking ticket

rows.label: Day 3
cells: Talks only about troponin numbers and ejection fraction

rows.label: Day 4
cells: Asks the nurse to feed and bathe them, though able

exhibits.title: New diagnosis
exhibits.body: An 8-year-old child is admitted with new type 1 diabetes after weight loss and bedwetting. The child loves soccer and worries about "being different" at school. The parents both work.

rows.label: Development
cells: Reads well, likes to learn how things work, collects cards

cells: Has no school nurse on site daily

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
